'''The Shri Ram Centre for Performing Arts''' (SRCPA) commonly referred as '''Shri Ram Centre''', is one of [[Delhi]]'s noted theatre organisation and [[theatre]] venues.<ref name="a259"/><ref name="m863">{{cite web | title=Theatres of Independence| author=Aparna Bhargava Dharwadker|year =2009 |isbn=158729642X| url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/Theatres_of_Independence/mLQaz-12Eo8C?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Shri+Ram+Centre+for+Performing+Arts&pg=PA92&printsec=frontcover|page=92|publisher =University of Iowa Press | access-date=2026-06-04}}</ref><ref name="b725">{{cite web | last=Bukhtiyar | first=Idrees | title=Mandi House: Where Delhi's theatre legacy comes alive | website=The Patriot | date=2025-03-23 | url=https://thepatriot.in/show-reel/mandi-house-where-delhis-theatre-legacy-comes-alive-67635 | access-date=2026-06-04}}</ref> It is situated at [[Mandi House]] on Safdar Hasmi Marg, [[New Delhi]], close to the [[Shriram Bharatiya Kala Kendra]], [[Triveni Kala Sangam]] and the [[National School of Drama]].<ref name="s978"/>

It is run by the [[Indian National Theatre]] Trust, established in 1958 the promotion of Art and Culture,  with people like [[Bharat Ram|Sheila Bharat Ram]], [[Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay]], [[Krishna Kripalani|Nandita Kriplani]] and [[Aditya Srivastava]] associated with it.<ref>[http://www.shriramcenterart.org/fac2.htm History] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727042343/http://www.shriramcenterart.org/fac2.htm|date=2011-07-27}} SRC website.</ref> The Centre runs a certified two-year-acting-course. The SRCPA Theatre Repertory Company started in 1980<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.shriramcenterart.org/act1.html|title=Repertory Performances|publisher=SRC}}</ref> and Puppet Theatre company, which over the years saw the rise of modern puppetry under puppeteer [[Dadi Pudumjee|Dadi Padamjee]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wepa.unima.org/en/dadi-pudumjee/|title = Dadi Pudumjee|date = 11 July 2017}}</ref>

== History ==

The present building of the Centre opened in the ’60s. The [[Brutalist]] building, built between 1966 and 1969, was designed by [[Shiv Nath Prasad]] and [[Mahendra Raj]]<ref name="y532">{{cite web | title=Shri Ram Center for Art and Culture | website=#SOSBRUTALISM | url=https://www.sosbrutalism.org/sixcms/detail.php?id=15889751 | access-date=2026-06-04}}</ref><ref name="a297">{{cite journal | last1=Prasad | first1=Shiv Nath | last2=Raj | first2=Mahendra | last3=Shetty | first3=Prasad | last4=Gulati | first4=Manish | last5=Kuriakose | first5=Biju | last6=Pandit | first6=Madhu | last7=Dasgupta | first7=Arunav | last8=Shivkumar | first8=Rohan | last9=Suresh | first9=Sabareesh | last10=Rewal | first10=Raj | title=Sri Ram Centre for Art and Culture | journal=Structural Engineering International | volume=1 | issue=3 | date=1972 | issn=1016-8664 | url=https://architexturez.net/doc/az-cf-123705 | access-date=2026-06-04 | page=}}</ref> with help from theatre doyen, [[Ebrahim Alkazi]], and was constructed under the overall supervision of industrialist Vinay Bharat Ram of [[Shriram Group]] ([[Delhi Cloth Mills|DCM Ltd.]]), from the industrialist family of [[Lala Shri Ram]]. The Shankar Lal Murli Dhar Auditorium is a proscenium theatre with a capacity of 375 people at two levels; 300 in the stall & 75 in the balcony.<ref name="d107">{{cite web | last=Varghese | first=Shiny | title=Building Blocks: Setting the Stage | website=The Indian Express | date=2018-05-06 | url=https://indianexpress.com/article/express-sunday-eye/building-blocks-setting-stage-the-shri-ram-centre-5164647/ | access-date=2026-06-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dcmtextiles.com/ceoprofile.asp|title=CEO Profile|publisher=DCM Textiles|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101211084620/http://www.dcmtextiles.com/ceoprofile.asp|archivedate=2010-12-11}}</ref> The building also had basement theatre which closed after a few decades, due to municipality regulations.<ref name="p159">{{cite web | title=This theatre of the absurd | website=The Times of India | date=2010-04-17 | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/this-theatre-of-the-absurd/articleshow/5824392.cms | access-date=2026-06-15}}</ref>

== Repertory ==

The SRCPA Repertory was set up in 1980 by theatre director Rajinder Nath.<ref name="toi"/> Presently, the Repertory is a full-time professional resident theatre company, performing regularly in Delhi and in other parts of the country. The company comprises 14 artists and a resident director namely, Sameep Singh (Chief of Repertory)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.outlookindia.com/newsscroll/new-production-of-vijay-tendulkars-1981-play-to-explore-complexities-of-homosexual-relationships/1536527|title=New production of Vijay Tendulkar's 1981 play to explore complexities of homosexual relationships}}</ref>

Over the years, the SRC Repertory Company has been working with directors like Rajinder Nath (1976-1981, 1983–89),<ref name="toi">{{cite web | title=Rajinder Nath, who shaped city theatre scene, no more | website=The Times of India | date=2025-07-25 | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/rajinder-nath-who-shaped-city-theatre-scene-no-more/articleshow/122887827.cms | access-date=2026-06-04}}</ref> Ranjit Kapoor,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.delhievents.com/2014/05/shri-ram-centre-repertory-presents-kiss.html|title = Shri Ram Centre Repertory presents 'Janpath Kiss' Hindi Play as part of Summer Weekend Theatre Festival at Shri Ram Center for Performing Arts (SRCPA), 4, Safdar Hashmi Marg > 7pm on 31st May & 1st June 2014 | date=June 2014 }}</ref> [[B.V.
